Mail-in ballot applications for the November 3rd, 2026 General Election must be received by 5pm October 27th. Mail-in ballots must be received by 8pm on November 3rd in order to be counted.

Voting By Mail Process

All registered voters can request a no-excuse mail-in ballot. You do not have to provide a reason for why you want to vote-by-mail; this means you can just request a mail-in ballot and do not need to request an absentee ballot regardless of the reason for voting by mail. You can apply online (https://nam10.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.pavoterservices.pa.gov%2FOnlineAbsenteeApplication%2F%23%2FOnlineMailInBegin&data=05%7C02%7Cigarcia-hernandez%40lwv.org%7C2d2b58307f1848fe94cd08dce0aebb2f%7C90befbfe6dce4edfba8a35fb67131124%7C1%7C1%7C638632288294061514%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=3Kaa3jqROyRJjes9lMQSs87DWEECGQD8r7ibjv7OB3Q%3D&reserved=0), by paper form (available in English (https://nam10.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.pa.gov%2Fen%2Fsearch.html%23q%3DPADOS_MailInApplication.pdf&data=05%7C02%7Cigarcia-hernandez%40lwv.org%7C2d2b58307f1848fe94cd08dce0aebb2f%7C90befbfe6dce4edfba8a35fb67131124%7C1%7C1%7C638632288294074502%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=DmQPpHfIjv9tEORj7S2s%2F7xlMGHuFnKd88Ry3lXyCRc%3D&reserved=0) and Spanish (https://nam10.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.pa.gov%2Fen%2Fsearch.html%23q%3DPADOS_MailInApplication_Spanish.pdf&data=05%7C02%7Cigarcia-hernandez%40lwv.org%7C2d2b58307f1848fe94cd08dce0aebb2f%7C90befbfe6dce4edfba8a35fb67131124%7C1%7C1%7C638632288294087321%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=UKdjnrq7E2oxrAMD2mxP%2ByzV5RZRS6ZX5yu62tz7Bbc%3D&reserved=0)), in person at your County Election Office (https://nam10.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fabsentee.vote411.org%2Fvote%2Feoddomestic.htm%3F_ga%3D2.6419642.961449.1727100920-889989650.1701105430&data=05%7C02%7Cigarcia-hernandez%40lwv.org%7C2d2b58307f1848fe94cd08dce0aebb2f%7C90befbfe6dce4edfba8a35fb67131124%7C1%7C1%7C638632288294100758%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=axEcqaohJAg%2B08LMqF6dcNhFM82YbzC0VT1q4EazHyI%3D&reserved=0), or by sending a signed letter to the office. The deadline to request a mail-in ballot is 7 days before the election, and completed ballots must be received by 8:00 pm Election Day to be counted. Voters are advised to closely follow the instructions on their mail-in ballots.

You can track your mail ballot on your Department of State’s website (https://nam10.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.pavoterservices.pa.gov%2Fpages%2Fballottracking.aspx&data=05%7C02%7Cigarcia-hernandez%40lwv.org%7C2d2b58307f1848fe94cd08dce0aebb2f%7C90befbfe6dce4edfba8a35fb67131124%7C1%7C1%7C638632288294113764%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=YLGbxb310Bb%2BA%2FyOEU4Ct8bHiZ5YQUelC0Fkvfqqphw%3D&reserved=0). Mail ballots are counted starting on Election Day.

Emergency Absentee Ballot

In case of an unexpected illness, disability, or emergency after the absentee ballot deadline, you can request an emergency absentee ballo (https://www.pa.gov/en/agencies/vote.html#emergency%20absentee)t.

If you requested an absentee ballot but decide to vote in person:

- If you've already submitted your mail-in or absentee ballot, you cannot vote at the polls.
- If you haven’t returned your mail-in ballot, you can either:

1. Bring your ballot and return envelope to your polling place to be voided. After signing a declaration, you'll vote a regular ballot.
2. If you don’t surrender your mail-in ballot, you’ll vote by provisional ballot, which will be counted after verifying you didn’t vote-by-mail.

For specifics, you can find your local county clerk contact info here (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm).

Excused Absentee Ballot

You may now request your absentee ballot online! (https://www.pavoterservices.pa.gov/OnlineAbsenteeApplication/#/OnlineAbsentee) You can vote absentee if you are:

- A college student
- Out of town on Election Day
- Have a disability or illness that prevents you from getting to your polling place
- A member of the military
- Have a conflict due to a religious holiday

All registered PA voters can cast their ballot by mail. After applying, you can track the status of your ballot here (https://nam10.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.pavoterservices.pa.gov%2FPages%2FBallotTracking.aspx&data=02%7C01%7CMBrown%40lwv.org%7C9f6b204b560f403ef47808d8407b6963%7C90befbfe6dce4edfba8a35fb67131124%7C0%7C0%7C637330246081011962&sdata=7TQ1eBeMb8MyFVYVG1yPXe5huDChZU2EHsY%2BjltTOLQ%3D&reserved=0).

The deadline to apply for an absentee ballot is one week before Election Day.

When you apply for an absentee ballot you must provide a driver's license number or a Social Security Number. If you don't know have a driver's license or a Social Security Number you must present a copy of an acceptable photo ID.

If you are a UOCAVA voter, a voter with a disability or voters over 65 and affected by the Voting Accessibility for Elderly and Handicapped Act you do not need to provide any ID to apply for your absentee ballot.

Deadlines for returning your voted absentee ballot:

The deadline to return your ballot is 8pm on Election Day.

If you have an emergency and have not applied for an absentee ballot by the deadline, you may download and apply for an Emergency Absentee Ballot. This application must be notarized before it is submitted. More information about Emergency Absentee Ballots can be found here. (https://www.vote.pa.gov/Voting-in-PA/Pages/Mail-and-Absentee-Ballot.aspx#emergencyabsentee)

  Request your Ballot  (https://www.pavoterservices.pa.gov/OnlineAbsenteeApplication/#/OnlineAbsenteeBegin)
Ballot curing is when a voter corrects an issue with their ballot, so it can be counted.

For information on federal campaign contributions, please visit Open Secrets (http://www.opensecrets.org).

For information on state campaign contributions, please visit your state's resource. (http://www.dos.pa.gov/VotingElections/CandidatesCommittees/CampaignFinance/Pages/default.aspx)
Information on local, state and federal candidates and ballot measures may be available here. (https://www.vote411.org/vote411.org/ballot)

The next election dates can be found here https://www.vote411.org/pennsylvania.

Contact your local Board of Elections (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm), for information about local elections.
The polling places are open from 7:00 am to 8:00 pm.

You are a Military or Overseas voter if you are in uniformed services, living overseas OR a spouse or dependent of a uniformed services voter. To get registered and vote, you can utilize Overseas Vote Foundation. (https://voterhelpdesk.usvotefoundation.org/en/support/home)

If you have additional questions about elections and voting overseas you can use our state specific elections official directory or contact the Overseas Vote Foundation. (https://voterhelpdesk.usvotefoundation.org/en/support/home)
You can make sure we have safe, fair, and efficient elections for all. Become a poll worker toda (https://powerthepolls.org/lwv)y!

You can find your polling place by utilizing your state resource. (https://www.pavoterservices.pa.gov/Pages/PollingPlaceInfo.aspx)

If you have further questions on your polling place location, please contact your county clerk (https://www.overseasvotefoundation.org/vote/election-official-directory). (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm)

Pennsylvania is a “closed primary” state. In order to vote in the primary election, voters must be registered with a political party. Unaffiliated or independent voters are not able to participate in the primary.

If you have any questions about your state’s primary election, please contact your local election officials (https://absentee.vote411.org/vote/eoddomestic.htm).

To verify your voter registration status

  click here!  (https://www.pavoterservices.pa.gov/pages/voterregistrationstatus.aspx)
